hypotheses: A Republican strategy to block Obama's re-election
The Republican leaders justified their policy by the need to fight against the electoral fraud.
Well, the Brennan Center considers this last to be a myth and says that the electoral fraud is less frequent in the United States than the number of people who die as a result of a lightning strike.
In fact, the Republican lawyers have found only 300 cases of electoral fraud in the United States over the last ten years.
One thing is certain: those new provisions will have a negative effect on the participation rate.
In this sense, these measures will weaken the American democratic system.
In contrast to what happens in Canada, the states in the United States are responsible for the organization of federal elections in the United States.
And in the same line, a majority of American governments promulgated, from 2009, new laws that made the process of registration or voting more difficult.
This phenomenon has spread since the November 2010 elections, which saw an increase of 675 new Republican representatives in 26 states.
Consequently, in 2011, 180 bills were introduced that restricted the exercise of the right of vote in 41 states.
The new electoral laws require that voters present a photo ID, in addition to a proof of American citizenship.

On the other hand, those laws reduce the period of advance voting, invalidate the right to register as an elector on the day of the vote, and take away the right to vote to citizens with criminal records.
Before the 2006 elections, no American state required that voters present a photo ID.
Indiana was the first state to demand it.
The Supreme Court of the United States confirmed in 2008 the constitutionality of the Indiana law.
Therefore, the Republican authorities rushed to extend that practice to other states.
In the last years these authorities have supported 34 laws to force the voters to present a document of identity with a photograph.
It is important to note that, unlike Quebec, American citizens do not have a universal identification document, such as the Social Security card.
In fact, 11% of the American citizens, or 21 million people in the voting age, do not have any government-issued photo ID.
On the other hand, five million new voters in 2012 lack an identity document with those characteristics.
But, often, the cost of obtaining the required identification document is more than one hundred dollars.
With this, the new restrictions affect disproportionally young people, minorities and people with low incomes.
In fact, 25% of African Americans, 15% of people earning less than $35,000 a year, 18% of citizens over the age of 65, and 20% of voters between the ages of 18 and 29 do not
And there is more.
In many states, students, the voters who vote the most for the Democratic candidates, cannot use the photo ID issued by their institution.
On the other hand, those same states authorize members of fishing or hunting clubs that usually vote for the Republican parties to use the documents issued by those clubs.
Before 2004, no state required the proof of citizenship to vote.
Arizona was the first state to present such an exigency.
Since 2011, a dozen states have adopted laws requiring voters to prove that they are American citizens.
Those measures clearly seek to limit the Hispanic vote.
It seems that two out of every three Hispanic voters support the Democratic Party.
On the other hand, the Republican legislators supported certain laws in 2011 that abolished the registration of voters on the same day of the vote in eight states.
In addition, they limited the right of people and groups to create a service to help voters who wanted to register.
These restrictions have consequences.
For example, in the general elections of 2004, the registration campaigns of voters contributed to the registration of around 10 million citizens.
The measures taken since 2009 have resulted in a decrease in the number of new voters registered in 2010 compared to 2006.
In addition, the Republican legislators adopted laws in other five states that favored the reduction of the advance voting period.
For example, in the 2008 elections in Florida, 33% of the voters who voted early were African American, while these last did not represent more than 13% of the state's voters.
In the case of the Spanish, it was exactly the same.
These do not represent more than 11% of the voters, which is equivalent to 24% of the citizens who vote in advance.
However, the whites, who represent 76% of the electorate, represent only 46% of the citizens who vote in advance.
Naturally, the Democratic legislators and their supporters have strongly opposed the adoption of laws that restrict the registration of voters.
In this sense, the Democratic governors have blocked several bills.
The US Attorney General intervened to suspend the most controversial laws.
In part, the damage was limited.
For example, only 16 of the 34 states adopted the law that required the presentation of a photo ID.
However, it is undeniable that the new rules adopted will complicate the exercise of the right to vote in 2012.
Democratic critics denounce the partisan character of the laws that have been voted, which it is clear that they are intended to influence the results of 2012 in the key states.
A Brennan Center report from 2011 shows that states that have adopted these laws represent 171 of the 270 votes needed in the electoral college to achieve the presidency.

To help their death be more comfortable.

53% of the patients admitted in the Victor-Gadboisarrivent hospital come from their homes and 47% of the hospital's patients are admitted from the hospital.
Problem of access to palliative care

77% of Canadians do not have access to palliative care, that is, care conceived to alleviate suffering when a patient reaches the terminal phase of his life, whether at home, in the hospital or in a care center.
And several organizations, such as the Victor-Gadbois Centre and the Grand Montréal Society of Hospice Care, specialize almost exclusively in the care of cancer patients.
It is precisely this relative lack of medical care in Quebec that makes many doctors specializing in palliative care fear the adoption of a law that regulates euthanasia and assisted suicide.
Since October, a manifesto signed by prominent palliative care experts, such as Dr. Balfour Mount and Dr. Bernard Lapointe, has circulated to show their opposition to such an initiative.
According to the Dr. Christiane Martel, the health system of Quebec is not sufficiently competent to ensure that anyone has the right to quality palliative care before proceeding with euthanasia.
"Recently", he says, "I have seen a patient suffering for 14 days in the Emergency room without the necessary measures being taken to alleviate her pain.
I fear that the patients want to die only because they are not receiving the proper care.
And in parallel, many oncologists insist with their patients until the last day, despite the worst prognoses.
Hélène Richard's hopes of survival were already at the lowest point when she left a tiring chemotherapy treatment.
"When I told my oncologist that I wanted to stop the treatment, she said that she was very sorry that I wanted to stop fighting", she says.
"However, she had told me that there was nothing else to do!"
There are no all-powerful care

Dr. Martel believes that 90% of the patients who request to die are grateful to their caregivers who have not attended to their demands once they have been relieved of their pain thanks to a team of palliative care.
However, it must be said that palliative care is not absolutely omnipotent in the treatment of pain.
According to Elsie Monereau, the Director of Grand Montréal's home care palliative care, patients do not respond to pain treatments in 8% of cases.
At the end of life, doctors usually resort to palliative sedation, which is used to sleep the patient until the moment of his death, either sporitally or permanently.
We cannot pretend that we do not understand that part of the suffering.
More often, the unhealed disease will have the possibility of having that palliative sedation.
The sick who are not relieved say all the same: "I want to die".
But that does not necessarily mean "I want euthanasia", it means "I want to be relieved".

The bitcoin price, after reaching the peak of $30 (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to $2 five months later, before returning today to around $10 (the prices are counted on the bitcoincharts.com page).
It is not impressive when compared with the changes in real money or in financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (ECB) was interested in it in an October report on virtual currencies.
In it, the bitcoin was described as "the virtual currency with the most success", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to the conventional coins".
Bitcoin is different from other systems of virtual currencies such as "credits", used to advance in a video game and that can be won playing or can be bought (and even sometimes exchanged).
The social network Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and tries the changes.
With the bitcoin, all the nodes of the network are at the same time the bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers of currency and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double-key encryption system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes of bitcoins are recorded in the public book, which is spread throughout the network.
The key point is to write that new transaction in that book.
This is a resolution of a mathematical challenge launched at the computers, and the winner, a kind of provisional central bank, will have the privilege of adding that line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique numerical fingerprint.
The computers "take" the new transaction and add a number before "breaking" the set.
The goal is to find the number that offers a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once the number is found, the other nodes verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then indelibly linked to the chain of other transactions; any modification would change the trace.

If, for committing a fraud, a user wanted to pay twice with the same money very quickly (less than ten minutes), the network would only accept one of the two transactions; the other would be left orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will receive 50 bitcoins.
To avoid inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but they are divisible up to the hundred millionth, leaving a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in computing power.
The life of the network has already had its ups and downs.
Websites that offer Bitcoin services have been attacked and bitcoins have been stolen in the deposit.
"The ruling used does not affect the same protocol", says Pierre Noizat, who has just launched Paymium, a real currency payment company that uses the Bitcoin network.
The ECB also takes into account the possibility of white money through this anonymous service.
But the cash money has the same defect.
The heavy actors, such as Wikipedia, reject such payments.
Others, such as the Wordpress platform, accept them.
Recently, Adi Shamir and Dorit Ron, from the Weizmann Institute in Israel, analyzed the book of accounts and showed that around 80% of bitcoins do not circulate.
The "big sales" were launched in November.
"They changed 30,000 dollars", says Jon Holmquist, who works for Coinabul, which converts bitcoins into gold.
Pierre Noizat, the author of a pedagogical book on that currency, believes quite a lot in the potential of this technology in addition to the network of transactions.
His system, Paytunia, is equivalent to a credit card (in real currency) or a mobile payment without contact, but uses Bitcoin to validate transactions, which are thus cheaper.
The carrier, in addition, manages his identity and can therefore remain in the anonymity.
The system is easy to put into operation in stores, which do not have to install new terminals or software.
All that is needed is a location that a phone can "photograph and recognize", says Pierre Noizat, who says he has thousands of users.
A general movement of review of hierarchical systems to more horizontal systems is underway.
"It will take time for Bitcoin to be accepted, but in 2013 it could be a change", predicts.
On the other hand, in his report the ECB will re-evaluate the various risks, which are considered high today, in case of success of this currency.

It is a new double or nothing to the President Mohammed Morsi.

The surprise announcement on Wednesday, when the Constituent Assembly voted on its final text the next day.

This new initiative has only increased the division in the country.
For his opponents, the President continues his "autocratic delirium" and continues to "betray his word" and "trample on the right".
On behalf of his supporters, it is assured that this is a measure to end the institutional and political crisis more quickly and to accelerate the transition process.
In the next fifteen days, a referendum should be organized.
A very short time that forces the Brothers to renounce their project of explaining the text, article by article, to the Egyptians.
For the President, it is also a way of recovering popular and democratic legitimacy while the controversy causes havoc throughout the country.
Mohammed Morsi seems to be convinced that the Egyptians will vote for him, as he said in an interview with the American magazine Time.

Considering that this resource has been voted for very quickly, it contains an ultimatum for the Egyptian people: "vote my text or I keep the full powers", powers that supposedly will end with the adoption of the Constitution.
It is in this strange atmosphere in which 85 members of this Constituent Assembly, the majority of which is Islamist, voted the text yesterday.
The majority of liberals did not attend the call.
In the middle of November, a little before the declaration of the constitution, they had closed the door because they thought they could not defend their points of view.

In order to achieve the necessary quorum, yesterday morning 11 people, substitute members, were added hastily.

The text, which was still being voted on yesterday afternoon, consists of 234 articles.
Article 2, the subject of all eyes, is still ultimately identical to that of the 1971 Constitution, which stipulated that "the principles of Sharia constitute the main source of law."

Salafist parties, who see the establishment of Islamic law as a fundamental reivindication, hoped that they could replace "the principles" with "the rules", which would have allowed a more strict application.

The liberals accuse him of hypocrisy and consider that it is nothing more than a publicity stunt.

According to the Egyptian expert Sophie Pommier, it is worrying because "the people called to speak are not elected and have no democratic legitimacy.

"At the moment, there is no concrete religious involvement.

The announcement of the probable discovery of the Higgs boson generated a great shock last summer, and for good reason.

The same thing happens with the Higgs boson, with the difference that it is another field, the Higgs field, which needs to be "disordered" for this boson to appear.

The opposite to current exchange rates based on central banks, the identified transactions and processing charges between the parties.
In addition, as often happens in technologies, the political vision is palpable: the conviction that the current monetary system, composed of banking monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, Bitcoin, invented by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is a virtual currency convertible to dollars, euros, etc., and a secure exchange protocol in the way of BitTorrent, which allows the exchange of files on an equal footing.
Thanks to 15,000 computers on the network, 200,000 transactions have been recorded.
And around a thousand websites accept bitcoins as donations or as a form of payment.

The bitcoin price, after reaching a high of 30 dollars (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to 2 dollars five months later, before returning today to around 10 dollars (the prices are counted on the bitcoincharts.com page).
It is not impressive when compared to the changes in real money or in financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (BCE) was interested in it in a report on virtual currencies published in October.
In it, the bitcoin was described as "the virtual currency with the most success", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to the conventional coins".
Bitcoin differs from other systems with types of virtual currencies such as "credits", used to advance in a video game and can be won by playing or can be bought (and even in some cases exchanged).
Facebook, a social network, also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with changes.
With Bitcoin, all nodes of the network are simultaneously bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers of currency and buyers and sellers.
How does this network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double-key encryption system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes of bitcoins are recorded in the public book of accounts, which is spread throughout the network.
The key point is to write this new transaction in that book.
This is the solution to a mathematical challenge launched at computers, and the winner, a kind of provisional central banker, will have the privilege of adding that extra line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique numerical signature.
The computers "catch" the new transaction and add a number before "cut" the set.
The objective is to find the number that offers a particular trace (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then inseparably linked to the chain of other transactions; any modification would change the trail.

Yes, to commit a fraud, a user would want to pay two times with the same money very quickly (less than ten minutes), the network would only accept one of the two transactions; the other would be orphaned, since both have different traces.
The computer that solves the challenge will be worth 50 bitcoins.
To avoid inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but they are divisible to the hundred millionth, which leaves a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in the power of calculation.
The life of the network has already had its ups and downs.
Web sites offering Bitcoin services have been attacked and Bitcoins have been stolen from deposit.
"The ruling does not affect the same protocol", says Pierre Noizat, who has just launched Paymium, a real money payment company that uses the Bitcoin network.
The ECB also takes into account the possibility of anonymous money laundering through this service.
But cash money has the same defect.
The heavy actors, such as Wikipedia, reject this type of payment.
Others, such as the Wordpress platform, are accepted.
Recently, Adi Shamir and Dorit Ron, from the Weizmann Institute in Israel, analyzed the book of accounts and showed that around 80% of bitcoins are not circulating.
In November, the "big sales" were launched.
"30,000 dollars were changed", Jon Holmquist, who works for Coinabul, that converts bitcoins into gold, is elated.
Pierre Noizat, author of a pedagogical book on that currency, believes quite in the potential of this technology in addition to the network of transactions.

The opposite to the current monetary exchanges, based on central banks, are the identified transactions and the processing charges between the parties.
In addition, as often happens in technologies, the political vision is palpable: the conviction that the current monetary system, composed of banking monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, Bitcoin, invented by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is at the same time a virtual currency convertible to dollars, euros, etc. and a secure exchange protocol in the way of BitTorrent, which allows the exchange of files on an equal basis.
Thanks to 15,000 computers in the network, there have been around 200,000 transactions.
And around a thousand websites accept bitcoins as donations or as a form of payment.

The bitcoin price, after reaching a peak of 30 dollars (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to 2 dollars five months later, before returning today to around 10 dollars (the prices are counted on the bitcoincharts.com page).
It is not impressive at the moment if we compare it with the real world changes in currency or in financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (BCE) was interested in it in an October report on virtual currencies.
In it, the bitcoin was described as "the most successful virtual currency", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to conventional coins".

Bitcoin is different from other systems with types of virtual currencies such as "credits", used to advance in a video game and that can be won by playing or can be bought (and even sometimes exchanged).
Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with the changes.
With the bitcoin, all the nodes of the network are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers of currency and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users takes place in reality between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double-key encryption system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public book of accounts, which is spread across the network.
The key point is to write that new transaction in that book.
This is the resolution of a mathematical challenge launched to the computers and the winner, a kind of provisional central banker, will have the privilege of adding that line.
It is a phase of file shredding, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique digital fingerprint.
The computers "catch" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The aim is to find the number that offers a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes easily verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then inextricably linked to the chain of other transactions; any modification would change the trace.

Yes, in order to commit a fraud, a user would want to pay twice with the same money very quickly (in less than ten minutes), the network would only accept one of the two transactions; the other would remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will receive 50 bitcoins.
In order to avoid inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but they are divisible to the hundredth of a million, leaving a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in the power of calculation.
The life of the network has already its ups and downs.

With Bitcoin, pay and sell without banks
In contrast to current interbank transactions, based on central banks, the identified transactions and processing charges between the parties.
In addition, as often happens in technology, the political vision is palpable: the conviction that the current monetary system, composed of bank monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, Bitcoin, invented by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is at the same time a virtual currency convertible to dollars, euros, etc. and a secure exchange protocol in the way of BitTorrent, which allows the exchange of files on an equal basis.
Thanks to 15,000 computers in the network, more than 200,000 transactions have been registered.
And around a thousand websites accept bitcoins as donations or as a form of payment.
The bitcoin price, after reaching a peak of $30 (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to $2 five months later, before returning today to around $10 (the prices are reported on the bitcoincharts.com page).
It is nothing impressive when compared with the world changes in real money or in financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (ECB) was interested in it in an October report on virtual currencies.
In it, the bitcoin was described as "the most successful virtual currency", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to conventional coins".
Bitcoin is different from other virtual currency systems like "credits" used to advance in a video game and that can be won by playing or can be bought (and even sometimes traded).
The social network Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and tries to make the changes.
With bitcoin, all the nodes of the network are at the same time accounting books, verifiers, currency emitters and buyers and sellers.
How does this network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a system of double-key encryption.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes of bitcoins are recorded in the public account book, which is spread throughout the network.
The key event consists in writing this new transaction in this book.
This is a resolution of a mathematical challenge launched at computers and the winner, a kind of provisional central bank, will have the privilege of adding that extra line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, i.e. transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique numerical signature.
The computers "take" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The objective is to find the number that offers a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once the number is found, the other nodes verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then indelibly linked to the chain of other transactions; any modification would change the trace.

Yes, in order to commit a fraud, a user would like to pay twice with the same money very quickly (less than ten minutes), the network will only accept one of the two transactions; the other will remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will receive 50 bitcoins.
To avoid inflation, this reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is, therefore, limited to 21 million, but they are divisible to the hundred-millionth, which leaves a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in the power of calculation.
The life of the network has already had its ups and downs.
Websites that offer services for Bitcoin have been attacked and bitcoins have been stolen from deposit.
"The decision used does not affect the same protocol", says Pierre Noizat, who just launched Paymium, a real money payment company that uses the Bitcoin network.
The ECB also takes account of the possibility of anonymous money laundering through this service.
But the cash money has the same defect.
The heavy actors, such as Wikipedia, reject such payments.
Others, like the Wordpress platform, are accepted.
Recently, Adi Shamir and Dorit Ron, from the Weizmann Institute in Israel, analyzed the book of accounts and showed that about 80% of bitcoins are not circulating.
In November, the "big sales" were launched.
"We changed 30,000 dollars", is happy Jon Holmquist, who works for Coinabul, which converts bitcoins into gold.
Pierre Noizat, author of a pedagogical book on that currency, believes quite a bit in the potential of this technology in addition to the network of transactions.
His system, Paytunia, is equivalent to a credit card (in real currency) or a mobile payment without contact, but uses Bitcoin to validate transactions, which are thus cheaper.
The carrier, in addition, manages his identity and can therefore remain anonymous.
The system is easy to set up in stores, which do not have to install new terminals or software.
All they need is a phone number that can "photograph and recognize" it, says Pierre Noizat, who claims to have thousands of users.
There is a general movement to review hierarchical systems to more horizontal systems.
"It will be a long time before Bitcoin is accepted, but in 2013 there could be a change", predicts.
On the other hand, in his report the ECB will revise the various risks, which are currently considered high, in the event that this currency succeeds.

A Constitution with a knife in Egypt
It is a new double or nothing to the President Mohammed Morsi.
While Egypt is more divided than ever in terms of the constitutional declaration, which gives it provisional powers, he decided to play everything for everything.
The surprise announcement on Wednesday, when he announced that the Constituent Assembly would vote on his final text on the following day.
Just a week ago, the Head of State had given two months more to this Assembly to finish its work.
And almost two years ago Egypt has used a provisional text, several times modified, which weakens the institutional stability and leads to judicial disputes.
This new initiative has only increased the division in the country.
For his opponents, the President continues his "autocratic delusion" and continues to "defile his word" and "trample on the right".
On behalf of his supporters, it is assured that this is a measure to end the institutional and political crisis more quickly and to speed up the transition process.
In the next 15 days, a referendum should be organized.
A very short time that forces the Brothers to renounce their project of explaining the text, one article at a time, to the Egyptians.
For the President, it is also a way of recovering a popular and democratic legitimacy while the controversy causes havoc throughout the country.
Mohammed Morsi appears to be convinced that the Egyptians will vote in his favor, as he said in an interview with the American weekly Time.

Considering that this resource has been voted on with great speed, it contains an ultimatum for the Egyptian people: "or vote my text or I maintain the full powers", powers that supposedly will be terminated with the adoption of the Constitution.
It is in this strange atmosphere that 85 members of this Constituent Assembly, most of them Islamic, voted the text yesterday.
Most liberals did not attend the call.
In mid-November, a little before the declaration of the constitution, they had closed the door because they thought they could not defend their points of view.
The representatives of human rights, religious minorities and civil society did the same.
In order to achieve the necessary quorum, 11 members, substitute members, were added hastily yesterday morning.
Some of them are very close to the Muslim Brotherhood.
As expected, the articles voted on have been voted on unanimously.

On the other hand, the commentators find it amusing that one of the few differences of the day has been expressed practically at the time of prayer, so much so that several members of the committee thought that the Constitution's clock was wrong.
The text, which was still being voted on yesterday afternoon, consists of 234 articles.
Article 2, which has been the subject of all eyes, is still identical to the 1971 Constitution, which stipulated that "the principles of Sharia constitute the main source of law".

Salafi parties, who consider the establishment of Islamic law a fundamental reivindications, hoped that "the principles" could be replaced by "the rules", which would have allowed a more strict application.
For the Islamicists, that this article has not been modified is a guarantee of their good intentions and respect for the other components of the Egyptian society.
Liberals accuse him of hypocrisy and consider that it is just a publicity stunt.
According to them, the Islamicization of the Constitution is done through other articles.
They refer, in particular, to Article 220, which confers a consultative role on the Al-Azhar University, in particular for anyone who has to confirm their conformity with the laws of the Sharia.
According to the expert in Egypt Sophie Pommier, it is alarming because "the people called to speak are not elected and have no democratic legitimacy.
Here we glimpse the premises of a theocracy.
The fears of the liberals are also increased by the fact that the next university president will be much less moderate than the current one.
"For now, there is no concrete religious implication.
With this Constitution we are in the civil state.

Most of the lawyers who have worked on this text are not ulemas but university professors, some of them trained in the French system, says Alexis Blouet, who is preparing a thesis on the Egyptian constitutional transition.
But he admits that there may be some ambiguity around Article 220, since the terms used imitate the religious vocabulary.
"We refer specifically to the term "iqh" [Islamic jurisprudence, ndlr].
And the question that could be asked in the future is to what extent are civil judges competent to speak on this matter.
Beyond its religious character, the text voted yesterday has received many criticisms that refer to the powers extended to the President of the Republic.
The Muslim Brotherhood will claim that they are few in comparison with what they were during the previous regime.

Do you want to take the test or not?
We have asked for advice from two experts.
In the studies conducted in the United States, a large number of infections were detected among the sample groups, so it is difficult to interpret those data and make firm recommendations.
In addition, the European study showed a certain difference in mortality among patients who had undergone the detection and those who had not.
The study, with a 12-year follow-up, also showed that there is a 30-40% chance of developing metastases if the test of detection has not been carried out.
Therefore, I recommend the test from age 50, or from age 40 if your father has suffered prostate cancer.
African American men have a higher risk.
The key is to make a good decision once the cancer has been detected.
There are aggressive cancers and other cancers that are benign.

It is really necessary to make the patient understand the degree of risk of his cancer. All possible options must be offered to him and not necessarily to treat prostate cancer that does not threaten long-term life, in which it is better to opt for active monitoring of the disease.
Today, many men who have been diagnosed with cancer are not treated, because the cancer is not aggressive and does not pose a risk to their life.
In place of this, we suggest active monitoring of the disease and, if it progresses, we offer treatment.
We are deciding more and more precisely who should or should not be treated.

The opposite to the current monetary exchanges, based on central banks, are the identified transactions and the processing charges between the parties.
In addition, as often happens in technology, the political vision is palpable: the conviction that the current monetary system, composed of banking monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, Bitcoin, invented by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is at once a virtual currency convertible to dollars, euros, etc. and a secure exchange protocol in the way of BitTorrent, which allows for equal exchange of files.
Thanks to 15,000 computers on the network, 20,000 transactions have been recorded.
And close to one thousand websites accept bitcoins as donations or as a payment method.

The bitcoin price, after reaching the peak of 30 dollars (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to 2 dollars five months later, before returning to around 10 dollars (the prices are counted on the bitcoincharts.com website).
It is not impressive when compared to the real world changes in currency or in financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (ECB) was interested in it in an October report on virtual currencies.
In it, bitcoin was described as "the most successful virtual currency", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to conventional coins".
Bitcoin differs from other virtual currency systems like "credits" used to advance in a video game and can be won by playing or purchased (even in some cases exchanged).
The social network Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with changes.
With bitcoin, all the nodes of the network are simultaneously bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers of currency and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double-key encryption system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes of bitcoins are recorded in the public book, which is spread throughout the network.
The key point is to write that new transaction in that book.
This passes through the resolution of a mathematical challenge launched at computers, and the winner, a kind of provisional central banker, will have the privilege of adding that extra line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique digital fingerprint.
The computers "catch" the new transaction and add a number before "breaking" the whole thing.
The objective is to find the number that gives a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes easily verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then indestructibly linked to the chain of other transactions; any modification would change the trace.

Yes, in order to carry out a fraud, a user would want to pay twice with the same money very quickly (in less than ten minutes), the network would only accept as valid one of the two transactions; the other would remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will receive 50 bitcoins.
To avoid inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but they are divisible up to the hundred-millionth, leaving a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also evident in each increase in computing power.
The life of the network has already its ups and downs.
Web sites offering services for Bitcoin have been attacked and bitcoins in deposit have been stolen.
"The decision used does not affect the same protocol", says Pierre Noizat, who just launched Paymium, a real currency payment company that uses the Bitcoin network.
In addition, the ECB considers the possibility of anonymous money laundering through this service.

Thanks to 15,000 computers on the network, more than 200,000 transactions have been recorded.

The bitcoin price, after reaching a high of 30 dollars (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to 2 dollars five months later, before returning today to around ten dollars (the prices are counted on the bitcoincharts.com page).

However, the European Central Bank (ECB) paid attention to him in an October report on virtual currencies.

Bitcoin differs from other virtual currency systems such as "credits", used to advance in a video game and which can be earned by playing or bought (even in some cases traded).
Facebook, a social network, also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with changes.
With bitcoin, all nodes of the network are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers of currency and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information linked to this transaction is signed electronically through a double-key encryption system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public book, which is spread throughout the network.
The key point is to write that new transaction in that book.
This passes through the resolution of a mathematical challenge launched at computers, and the winner, a kind of temporary central bank, will have the privilege of adding that additional line.
It is a stage of file fragmentation, i.e., the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique digital signature.
The computers "catch" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The goal is to find the number that offers a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once the number is found, the other nodes verify easily that it is the good one.
The transaction is then indelibly linked to the chain of other transactions; any modification would change the signature.

Yes, to commit fraud, a user would want to pay twice with the same money very quickly (in less than ten minutes), the network would only accept one of the two transactions; the other would remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will be worth 50 bitcoins.
To avoid inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins currently in circulation is limited to 21 million, but they are divisible up to the hundredth millionth, leaving a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is revealed in each increase in computing power.
The life of the network has already had its ups and downs.

With Bitcoin, pay and sell without banks
Contrary to current exchange rates, which are based on central banks, transactions identified and processing costs between the parties.
In addition, as is often the case in technology, political vision is palpable: the conviction that the current monetary system, composed of bank monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, Bitcoin, created by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is at the same time a virtual currency that can be converted to dollars, euros, etc., and a secure exchange protocol in the way of BitTorrent, which allows for equal exchange of files.
200,000 transactions have been registered thanks to 15,000 computers on the network.
And close to a thousand websites accept bitcoins as donations or as a form of payment.

The bitcoin price, after reaching a peak of $30 (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to $2 five months later, before returning today to hover around $10 (the prices are tracked on the bitcoincharts.com page).
It is not impressive compared to global changes in real currency or financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (ECB) was interested in it in a report on virtual currencies published in October.
In it, bitcoin was described as "the virtual currency with the most success", "which competes with the dollar or euro" and "similar to conventional coins".
Bitcoin is different from other virtual currency systems such as "credits", used to advance in a video game and can be won by playing or can be bought (and even in some cases can be exchanged).
The social network Facebook developed also this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with changes.
With Bitcoin, all nodes of the network are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, currency emitters and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a system of double-encryption.
The network can verify the authenticity of transactions.
Thanks to the file, it is also possible to ensure that changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public account, which is spread throughout the network.
The key point is to write that new transaction in that book.
This is a solution to a mathematical challenge set for computers and the winner, a kind of temporary central bank, will have the privilege of adding that extra line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, i.e., transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique digital fingerprint.
The computers "take" the new transaction and add a number before "shooting" the set.
The aim is to find the number that offers a particular (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes verify easily that it is the good one.
The transaction is then inescapably linked to the chain of other transactions; any change would alter the trace.

Yes, in order to commit a fraud, a user would like to pay two times with the same money very fast (in less than ten minutes), the network will accept only one of the two transactions; the other will remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will be rewarded with 50 bitcoins.
To avoid inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but are divisible to the hundred millionth, which leaves a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in computing power.
The life of the network has already had its ups and downs.
Websites that offer services for Bitcoin have been attacked and bitcoins have been stolen.
"The decision used does not affect the same protocol", says Pierre Noizat, who has just launched Paymium, a real currency payment company that uses the Bitcoin network.
The ECB takes into account, in addition, the possibility of "wholesale" money through this anonymous service.

The actors of weight, such as Wikipedia, reject such payments.
Others, such as the platform Wordpress, accept.
Recently, Adi Shamir and Dorit Ron, from the Weizmann Institute in Israel, analyzed the book of accounts and showed that 80% of bitcoins circulate.
In November, " giant sales" were launched.
"30,000 dollars were changed", joyously says Jon Holmquist, who works for Coinabul, which converts bitcoins into gold.

I recommend that the test be done in any case.

The Higgs boson in detail
The announcement of the probable discovery of the Higgs boson generated a great stir last summer, and for good reason.
It is believed, indeed, that this boson is a participant in the mechanism responsible for the mass of everything that exists in the universe, nothing more and nothing less.

And what is more, it is the particle whose existence was predicted by the Standard Model: our best or "worse" explanation of the nature and behavior of matter, which has not yet been empirically observed.
But for physicists it is not yet clear that it is Higgs.
We know without doubt that there is a new particle and that it is very similar to the Higgs boson predicted by the standard model.
In addition, new data released this week at an important physics conference held in Kyoto seem to confirm that it is, although more data is needed to be completely sure.
However, we assume that it is Higgs, since the chances of being wrong seem few. We will see what it is about.
In this great world, there is a general and unavoidable law that implies that two things cannot be found in the same place at the same time.
There is no way to violate that rule and it is not worth trying too much, because it will end up hurting you.

Although the physics of particles is a very complex world, it has been shown that there is also a law of this kind: the Pauli exclusion principle, which stipulates that two particles cannot occupy the same space at the same time if they are in the same "quantum state"; a "state" which, in
Physicists classify particles into two categories.
On the one hand, we find the good citizens called fermions, who obey the principle of Pauli wisely.
And there are the anarchists, a dirty panda of anarchy that has no respect for anything, or at least not for this principle, which means that they can be in the same place and at the same time.

According to the web page The Particle Adventure of the Berkeley Laboratories, which by the way is extraordinary, the bosons are divided into two groups: mesons, of which we will not speak here, and the "force particles", with which the great forces of nature propagate and with which the Higgs boson is somehow
These bosons, here, it would be important to underline, are not the exotic creatures we might think.
In fact, if he can read this article, it is thanks to an extraordinarily banal boson: the photon or the "light particle" that acts as the "message" of the electromagnetic force.
In fact, when a charged particle accelerates or changes direction, it "disorders" the electromagnetic field in that exact environment; a little like when you throw a stone into a pond.
In this "disorder" an electromagnetic wave (of light, of infrared, of ultraviolet, etc.) is born, and this wave is nothing but a photon; that is to say, one of the force carriers bosons.
More stable field
The same thing happens with the Higgs boson, with the difference that it is another field, the Higgs field, which needs to be "disordered" for this boson to appear.

Now, the Higgs field is much more stable than the electromagnetic field. To activate it, you need to reach extremely high energies, just like if you were in a frozen lake where only a heavy rock could slide across the surface.
Therefore, a huge particle accelerator like the one at CERN (the great hadron collider is a ring 27 km in circumference!) is needed to reach such levels of energy.
The analogy with the electromagnetic field is a new tool that explains the relationship between the Higgs and mass.
In fact, not all particles or materials interact with the electromagnetic field.
Some, like magnets, do it, but others don't: a piece of paper, for example, will never stick to the door of a refrigerator by itself.
And in the same way, not all particles interact with the Higgs field: those that do have mass, while the rest (for example, the photon, by the way) do not.
Now, what can all those investigations contribute?, asks Mrs. Plamondon.
For science, this is to verify the validity of the Standard Model (SM), and also allows physicists to scrutinize the differences between observations and predictions of the SM.
On the other hand, many want to see them, because the smallest difference could open a door to "new physics" that covers some holes in the model.

This, it has to be said, still has many shortcomings, such as not proposing any explanation of the gravity (oops!) or dark matter, which makes up around 80% of the matter in the Universe (another oops!).
But we have not found such differences in the CERN so far.
Consequences
The consequences of these investigations in our daily life are difficult to predict, but we do not believe that we are wrong when we say that they will not have any.
To see: at the beginning of the 1960s, the pioneers of the laser in the laboratories did not even suspect the revolution that their work would provoke.
They saw the scientific applications, but nothing else.

In fact, as the physicist Willard Boyle, who worked in Bell Laboratories where the laser was invented in 1960, and who made the first continuous laser (the first were pulsed) in 1962, at first the laser was more or less considered a "laboratory device".
Imagine...
And also, the applications can also come from all the instrumentation that surrounds the research.
For example, the same Willard Boyle developed a light detector in 1969 during his research in optics.
Although it was not his original intention, this detector is now used as a "eye" for all digital devices in the world, which earned him the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2009.
That does not mean, of course, that the activities of the LHC will necessarily transform our lives, but never know...

With Bitcoin, pay and sell without banks
The opposite to the current exchange rates based on central banks, the transactions identified and the processing charges between the parties.
In addition, as is often the case with technology, the political vision is palpable: the conviction that the current monetary system, composed of banking monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, Bitcoin, invented by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is at the same time a virtual currency convertible to dollars, euros, etc. and a secure exchange protocol in the way of BitTorrent, which allows the exchange of files on an equal basis.
More than 200,000 transactions have been registered thanks to 15,000 computers on the network.
And around a thousand websites accept bitcoins as donations or as a form of payment.
The bitcoin price, after reaching a peak of $30 (€23) in June 2011, fell to $2 five months later, before returning today to around $10 (the prices are registered on the bitcoincharts.com page).
It is not impressive when compared with the world changes in real money or in financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (ECB) was interested in it in a report on virtual currencies published in October.
In it, the bitcoin was described as "the most successful virtual currency", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to the conventional coins".
Bitcoin is different from other virtual currency systems such as "credits", used to advance in a video game and can be won by playing or can be bought (and even sometimes exchanged).
The social network Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with the changes.
With bitcoin, all the nodes of the network are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, currency issuers and buyers and sellers.
How does that network works?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double-key encryption system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public book of accounts, which is spread throughout the network.
The key point is to write that new transaction in that book.
This is a resolution of a mathematical challenge launched to the computers and the winner, a kind of provisional central bank, will have the privilege of adding that extra line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique digital signature.
The computers "catch" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The goal is to find the number that will give a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes will easily verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then irreversibly linked to the chain of other transactions; any change would alter the trace.

Yes, in order to commit a fraud, a user would like to pay twice with the same money very quickly (less than ten minutes), the network will only accept one of the two transactions; the other will remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will receive 50 bitcoins.
To avoid inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but they are divisible to the hundred-millionth, which leaves a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in computing power.
The life of the network has already had its ups and downs.
Web sites that offer services for Bitcoin have been attacked and bitcoins in deposit have been stolen.
"The ruling does not affect the same protocol", says Pierre Noizat, who has just launched Paymium, a real currency payment company that uses the Bitcoin network.
The ECB also takes into account the possibility of anonymous money laundering through this service.
But cash money has the same defect.
The heavy actors, such as Wikipedia, reject such payments.
Others, such as the Wordpress platform, accept them.
Recently, Adi Shamir and Dorit Ron, from the Weizmann Institute in Israel, analyzed the bookkeeping and showed that about 80% of bitcoins are not circulating.
In November, the "giant sales" were launched.
"30,000 dollars were changed", says Jon Holmquist, who works for Coinabul, which converts bitcoins into gold.
Pierre Noizat, author of a pedagogical book on that currency, believes quite a lot in the potential of this technology in addition to the network of transactions.
His system, Paytunia, is equivalent to a credit card (in real currency) or a mobile payment without contact, but uses Bitcoin to validate transactions, which are thus cheaper.
The carrier, in addition, manages his identity and can therefore remain anonymous.
The system is easy to set up in shops, which do not have to install new terminals or software.
All they need is a location that a phone can "photograph and recognize", says Pierre Noizat, who claims to have thousands of users.
There is a general movement for the review of hierarchical systems to more horizontal systems.
"It will take time for Bitcoin to be accepted, but in 2013 there could be a change", predicts.
On the other hand, in his report the ECB will review the various risks, which are considered high today, in case this currency succeeds.

A Constitution with a fork in Egypt
It is a new double or nothing to the President Mohammed Morsi.
While Egypt is more divided than ever in terms of the constitutional declaration, which gives it provisional powers, he decided to play the whole for the whole.
The surprise came on Wednesday when he announced that the Constituent Assembly would vote on its final text the next day.
Just a week ago, the Head of State had given two more months to this Assembly to finish its work.
And it has been almost two years since Egypt has used a provisional text, which has been modified several times, weakening the institutional stability and leading to judicial entanglements.
This new initiative has only increased the division in the country.
For his opponents, the President continues his "autocratic delirium" and continues to "betray his word" and "trample on the right".
On behalf of his supporters, it is assured that this is a measure to end the institutional and political crisis faster and to accelerate the transition process.
In the next 15 days, a referendum should be organized.
A very short time that forces the Brothers to renounce their project of explaining the text, article by article, to the Egyptians.
For the President, it is also a way to regain popular and democratic legitimacy while the controversy causes havoc throughout the country.
Mohammed Morsi seems to be convinced that the Egyptians will vote for him, as he said in an interview with the American magazine Time.

Considering that this resource has been voted on very quickly, it contains an ultimatum for the Egyptian people: "or vote my text or I keep the full powers", powers that supposedly will end with the adoption of the Constitution.
It is in this strange atmosphere that 85 members of this Constituent Assembly, most of them Islamist, voted the text yesterday.
Most liberals did not attend the call.
In mid-November, a little before the constitutional declaration, they had closed the door because they thought they could not make their views prevail.
The representatives of human rights, religious minorities and civil society did the same.
In order to reach the necessary quorum, 11 members, substitute members, were added hastily this morning.
Some of them are very close to the Muslim Brotherhood.
As was expected, the articles voted on have been voted for unanimously.

On the other hand, the commentators find it funny that one of the few differences of the day has been expressed practically at the time of prayer, so much so that several members of the committee thought that the clock of the Constituent was wrong.
The text, which was still being voted on yesterday afternoon, consists of 234 articles.
Article 2, the subject of all eyes, is still ultimately identical to that of the 1971 Constitution, which stipulated that "the principles of Sharia constitute the main source of law."

The Salafist parties, for whom the establishment of Islamic law is a fundamental demand, hoped that they could replace "the principles" with "the rules", which would have allowed a more strict application.
For the Islamicists, the fact that this article has not been modified is a guarantee of their good will and respect for the other components of Egyptian society.
The liberals accuse him of hypocrisy and consider that it is just a publicity stunt.
According to them, the Islamization of the Constitution is done through other articles.
They refer, in particular, to Article 220, which confers a consultative role to the Al-Azhar University, in particular for anyone who is to confirm their compliance with the laws of Sharia.
According to the Egypt specialist Sophie Pommier, it is alarming because "the people called to speak are not elected and have no democratic legitimacy.
Here we glimpse the premises of a theocracy.
The fears of the liberals are also increased by the fact that the next university president will be much less moderate than the current one.
"At the moment, there is no concrete religious implication.

The majority of the lawyers who have been working on that text are not ulemas but university professors, some of them trained in the French system", explains Alexis Blouet, who is preparing a thesis on the Egyptian constitutional transition.
But he admits that there may be some ambiguity around Article 220, since the terms used resemble the religious vocabulary.
"We are specifically referring to the term iqa [Islamic jurisprudence, ndlr].
And the question that could be raised in the future would be to what extent are the civil judges competent to speak on this matter.
Beyond its religious character, the text voted yesterday has received many criticisms that refer to the powers extended to the President of the Republic.
The Muslim Brothers will claim that they are few in comparison to those who were during the previous regime.
Another controversial point: the powers given to the army.
In accordance with the desire of the military, the review of the Defense Budget will not be submitted to Parliament, but to a National Defense Council.

The Higgs boson in detail
The announcement of the probable discovery of the Higgs boson generated a great stir last summer, and for good reason.
It is believed, in fact, that this boson is a participant in the mechanism responsible for the mass of everything that exists in the universe, nothing more and nothing less.

And what is more, it is the particle whose existence the standard model predicted: our best or "least bad" explanation of the nature and behavior of matter, which has not yet been empirically observed.
But for physicists it is not yet clear that it is the Higgs.
We know without a doubt that there is a new particle and that it is very similar to the Higgs boson predicted by the standard model.
In addition, new data released this week at an important physics conference held in Kioto seem to confirm that it is, although more data is needed to be completely sure.
However, we assume that it is Higgs, since the chances of being wrong seem few. We will see what it is about.
In this great world, there is a general and ineludible law that implies that two things cannot be found in the same place at the same time.
There is no way to violate that rule and it is not worth trying too hard, because it will end up hurting you.

Although the physics of particles is a very complex world, it has been demonstrated that there is also a law of this kind: the Pauli exclusion principle, which stipulates that two particles cannot occupy the same space at the same time if they are in the same "quantum state"; a "state" that, roughly
Physicists classify particles into two categories.
On the one hand, we find the good citizens called fermions, who obey the Pauli principle wisely.

And there are the anarchists, a dirty panda of anarcho-syndicalists who have no respect for anything, or at least not for this principle, which means that they can be found in the same place and at the same time.

According to the Particle Adventure web page of the Berkeley Laboratories, which is extraordinary, the bosons are divided into two groups: mesons, of which we will not speak here, and the "force particles", with which the great forces of nature propagate and with which the Higgs boson is in some way related.
These bosons, here, it would be important to underline, are not the exotic creatures that we might believe.
In fact, if he is able to read this article, it is thanks to an extraordinary particle: the photon or the "light particle" that acts as the "message" of the electromagnetic force.
In fact, when a charged particle accelerates or changes direction, it "disorders" the electromagnetic field in that precise environment; a little like when we throw a stone into a pond.
In this "disorder" an electromagnetic wave (of light, of infrared, of ultraviolet, etc.) is born, and this wave is nothing but a photon; that is, one of the bosons "carriers of force".
More stable field
The same thing happens with the Higgs boson, with the difference that it is another field, the Higgs field, which needs to be "disordered" for this boson to appear.
Now, the Higgs field is much more stable than the electromagnetic field. To activate it, you need to reach extremely high energies, just like trying to slide a heavy rock across a frozen lake.
Therefore, a huge particle accelerator like the CERN (the great hadron collider is a 27 km ring!) is needed to reach such levels of energy.
The analogy with the electromagnetic field is a new tool that explains the relationship between the Higgs and mass.
In fact, not all particles or all materials interact with the electromagnetic field.
Some, like magnets, do it, but others don't: a piece of paper, for example, will never stay stuck to the door of a refrigerator by itself.
And in the same way, not all particles interact with the Higgs field: those that do have mass, while the rest (like the photon, for example) do not.
Now, what can all those investigations contribute?, asks Mrs. Plamondon.
For science, this serves to verify the validity of the standard model (MS), and also allows physicists to scrutinize the differences between observations and predictions of the MS.
On the other hand, many wish that they could meet, for the slightest difference could open a door to "new physics" that covers certain holes in the model.

This, it has to be said, still has many shortcomings, such as not proposing any explanation at all relative to the gravity (¡ups!) or to the dark matter, which makes up around 80% of the matter of the Universe (¡another ups!).
But we have not found such differences in the CERN until now.
Consequences
The repercussions of these investigations in our daily life are difficult to predict, but we do not believe that we are wrong to say that it will not have any.
To see: at the beginning of the 1960s, laser pioneers in the laboratories did not even suspect in absolute terms the revolution that their work would provoke.
They saw the scientific applications, but nothing more.

In fact, as Willard Boyle, who worked at Bell Laboratories where the laser was invented in 1960, and who developed the first continuous laser (the first were pulsed) in 1962, said, the laser was more or less considered a "laboratory apparatus" at first
Imagine...
And also, the applications can come from all the instrumentation that surrounds the investigation.
For example, the same Willard Boyle developed a light detector in 1969 during his research in optics.
Although it was not his original intention, this detector now serves as a "eye" for all digital devices in the world, which earned him the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2009.
That does not mean, of course, that the activities of the LHC will necessarily transform our lives, but never know...

However, the European Central Bank (BCE) was interested in it in a report on virtual currencies published in October.

Bitcoin is different from other systems with types of virtual currency such as "credits", used to advance in a video game and that can be won by playing or can be bought (and even traded in some cases).
Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and treats the changes.
With bitcoin, all the network nodes are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, emitters of currency and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Every transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double-key encryption system.
The red can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes of bitcoins are recorded in the public book, which is spread throughout the network.
The key point is to write that new transaction in that book.
This is the resolution of a mathematical challenge launched at the computers and the winner, a kind of provisional central banker, will have the privilege of adding that extra line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique digital fingerprint.
The computers "catch" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The goal is to find the number that offers a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then indestructibly linked to the chain of other transactions; any modification would change the trail.

Yes, to commit a fraud, a user would want to pay twice with the same money very quickly (less than ten minutes), the network would only accept one of the two transactions; the other would remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will receive 50 bitcoins.
To avoid inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is, therefore, limited to 21 million, but are divisible to the hundred millionth, which leaves a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in the power of calculation.

With Bitcoin, pay and sell without banks
The opposite to the current exchange rates, based on central banks, the transactions identified and the processing charges between the parties.
In addition, as is often the case with technology, the political vision is palpable: the conviction that the current monetary system, composed of banking monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, Bitcoin, invented by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is at the same time a virtual currency convertible to dollars, euros, etc. and a secure exchange protocol in the way of BitTorrent, which allows the exchange of files on an equal basis.
Thanks to 15,000 computers on the network, 200,000 transactions have been recorded.
And close to a thousand websites accept bitcoins as donations or as a form of payment.
The bitcoin price, after reaching a peak of $30 (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to $2 five months later, before returning today to around $10 (the prices are tracked on the bitcoincharts.com page).
It is nothing impressive when compared to the changes in real money or financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (ECB) was interested in it in a report on virtual currencies published in October.
In it, the bitcoin was described as "the most successful virtual currency", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to the conventional coins".

Bitcoin is different from other systems with types of virtual currencies such as "credits", used to advance in a video game and that can be won by playing or can be bought (and even in some cases exchanged).
The social network Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with the changes.
With Bitcoin, all the nodes of the network are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers of currency and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a system of double-key encryption.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public book of accounts, which is spread throughout the network.
The key point is to write that new transaction in that book.
This is a solution to a mathematical challenge launched at the computers, and the winner, a kind of temporary central banker, will have the privilege of adding that extra line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique numerical signature.

The announcement of the probable discovery of the Higgs boson generated a great stir last summer, and for good reason.
It is believed, in fact, that this boson is a participant in the mechanism responsible for the mass of everything that exists in the universe, nothing more and nothing less.

But for physicists it is not yet clear that it is Higgs.
We know without doubt that there is a new particle and that it is very similar to the Higgs boson predicted by the standard model.
In addition, new data released this week at an important physics conference held in Kyoto seem to confirm that it is, although more data is needed to be completely sure.
However, we assume it is Higgs, since the chances of being wrong seem few. We will see what it is.
In this great world, there is a general and inescapable law that implies that two things cannot be found in the same place at the same time.
There is no way to violate that rule and you should not try too hard, because it will end up hurting you.

Although the physics of particles is a very complex world, it has been shown that it also has a law of these characteristics: the Pauli exclusion principle, which stipulates that two particles cannot occupy the same space at the same time if they are in the same "quantum state"; a "state" that consists,
Physicists classify particles into two categories.
On the one hand, we find the good citizens called fermions, who obey wisely the principle of Pauli.

According to the Berkeley Laboratory website, the particle is divided into two groups: mesons, of which we will not speak here, and the "force particles", with which the great forces of nature propagate and with which the Higgs boson is somehow related.

In fact, if he can read this article, it is thanks to a very unusual boson: the photon or the "light particle" that acts as the "message" of the electromagnetic force.
In fact, when a charged particle accelerates or changes direction, it "disorders" the electromagnetic field in that precise area; just like when we throw a stone into a pond.
In this "disorder" an electromagnetic wave (of light, of infrared, of ultraviolet, etc.) is born, and this wave is nothing but a photon; that is, one of the force carriers bosons.
More stable field
The same thing happens with the Higgs boson, with the difference that it is another field, the Higgs field, which needs to be "disordered" for this boson to appear.
Now, the Higgs field is much more stable than the electromagnetic field. To activate it, it requires extremely high energies, just like trying to slide a large rock across a frozen lake.
Therefore, it is necessary to have a huge particle accelerator like the one at CERN (the great hadron collider is a ring of 27 km in circumference!) to reach such levels of energy.
The analogy with the electromagnetic field is a new tool that explains the relationship between the Higgs and mass.
In fact, not all particles or materials interact with the electromagnetic field.

But we have not found such differences in the CERN so far.
Consequences

To see: at the beginning of the 60s, the pioneers of the laser in the laboratories did not even suspect in any way the revolution that their work would provoke.
They saw the scientific applications, but nothing more.

In fact, as the physicist Willard Boyle, who worked in Bell Laboratories, where the laser was invented in 1960, and who developed the first continuous laser (the first ones were pulsed) in 1962, initially the laser was more or less considered a "laboratory device
Imagine...
