In fact, Bitcoin, invented by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is at the same time a virtual currency convertible to dollars, euros, etc. and a secure exchange protocol in the way of BitTorrent, which allows the exchange of files on an equal basis.
Thanks to 15,000 computers on the network, there have been more than 200,000 transactions recorded.
And close to a thousand websites accept bitcoins as donations or as a form of payment.
The bitcoin price, after reaching a peak of $30 (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to $2 five months later, before returning to around $10 today, according to the bitcoincharts.com website.
It is not impressive when compared to the real world changes in currency or financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (ECB) was interested in it in an October report on virtual currencies.
In it, it was described as "the virtual currency with the most success", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to the conventional coins".
Bitcoin is different from other virtual currency systems such as "credits", used to advance in a video game and that can be won by playing or bought (and even in some cases traded).
Facebook, a social network, also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with the changes.
With bitcoin, all the nodes of the network are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers of currency and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double-key encryption system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public ledger, which is spread throughout the network.
The key point is to write that new transaction in that book.
This is a resolution of a mathematical challenge launched at the computers, and the winner, a kind of provisional central bank, will have the privilege of adding that extra line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique digital fingerprint.
The computers "catch" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The goal is to find the number that provides a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then inextricably linked to the chain of other transactions; any modification would change the trail.

Yes, in order to commit a fraud, a user would like to pay twice with the same money very quickly (less than ten minutes), the network will accept only one of the two transactions; the other will remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will receive 50 bitcoins.
To avoid inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but they are divisible to the hundred-millionth, leaving a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in computing power.
The life of the network has already had its ups and downs.
Web sites offering Bitcoin services have been attacked and bitcoins in storage have been stolen.

With Bitcoin, pay and sell without banks
The opposite to the current exchange rates, based on central banks, the transactions identified and the processing charges between the parties.
In addition, as is often the case with technology, the political vision is palpable: the conviction that the current monetary system, composed of bank monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, Bitcoin, invented by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is at the same time a virtual currency convertible to dollars, euros, etc. and a secure exchange protocol in the way of BitTorrent, which allows the exchange of files of equal to equal.
There have been 200,000 transactions recorded thanks to 15,000 computers on the network.
And around a thousand websites accept bitcoins as donations or as a form of payment.
The bitcoin price, after reaching a peak of $30 (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to $2 five months later, before returning today to around $10 (the prices are tracked on the bitcoincharts.com page).
It is not impressive when compared to the changes in real money or financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (ECB) was interested in it in an October report on virtual currencies.
In it, the bitcoin was described as "the most successful virtual currency", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to the conventional coins".

Bitcoin is different from other systems with types of virtual currency such as "credits", used to advance in a video game and that can be won by playing or can be bought (and even in some cases exchanged).
The social network Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with the changes.
With Bitcoin, all the nodes of the network are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers of currency and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a system of double-key encryption.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public book of accounts, which is distributed throughout the network.
The key point is to write that new transaction in that book.
This is a resolution of a mathematical challenge launched at the computers, and the winner, a kind of temporary central banker, will have the privilege of adding that additional line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique digital fingerprint.
The computers "catch" the new transaction and add a number before "cut" the set.
The goal is to find the number that will give a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes will verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then inextricably linked to the chain of other transactions; any change would alter the trace.

Yes, in order to commit a fraud, a user would like to pay twice with the same money very quickly (less than ten minutes), the network will only accept one of the two transactions; the other will remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will receive 50 bitcoins.
To avoid inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but they are divisible to the hundred-millionth, which leaves a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in computing power.
The life of the network has already had its ups and downs.
Web sites that offer services for Bitcoin have been attacked and bitcoins have been stolen from the deposit.
"The ruling used does not affect the same protocol", says Pierre Noizat, who just launched Paymium, a company that uses the Bitcoin network for real money payments.
The ECB also takes into account the possibility of a "black" money service through this anonymous service.

Others, such as the Wordpress platform, accept them.

With Bitcoin, pay and sell without banks
The opposite to the current exchange rates based on central banks, the identified transactions and the processing charges between the parties.
In addition, as is often the case with technology, the political vision is palpable: the conviction that the current monetary system, composed of bank monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, Bitcoin, invented by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is at the same time a virtual currency convertible to dollars, euros, etc. and a secure exchange protocol in the way of BitTorrent, which allows the exchange of files on an equal basis.
Thanks to 15,000 computers on the network, there have been more than 200,000 transactions.
And close to a thousand websites accept bitcoins as donations or as a form of payment.
The bitcoin price, after reaching a peak of $30 (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to $2 five months later, before returning today to around $10 (the prices are tracked on the bitcoincharts.com page).
It is not impressive when compared to the changes in real money or financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (ECB) was interested in it in an October report on virtual currencies.
In it, the bitcoin was described as "the most successful virtual currency", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to conventional coins".
Bitcoin differs from other virtual currency systems such as "credits", used to advance in a video game and that can be won by playing or can be bought (and even in some cases traded).
Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with the changes.
With bitcoin, all the nodes of the network are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers of currency and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double-key encryption system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public ledger, which is spread throughout the network.
The key point is to write that new transaction in that book.
This is a solution to a mathematical challenge launched at the computers, and the winner, a kind of provisional central banker, will have the privilege of adding that extra line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique digital signature.
The computers "catch" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The goal is to find the number that offers a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes easily verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then inextricably linked to the chain of other transactions; any change would alter the trail.

Yes, in order to commit fraud, a user would want to pay twice with the same money very quickly (less than ten minutes), the network would only accept one of the two transactions; the other would remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will receive 50 bitcoins.
To avoid inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but they are divisible to the hundred-millionth, leaving a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in computing power.
The life of the network has already had its ups and downs.
Web sites that offer services for Bitcoin have been attacked and bitcoins have been stolen from deposit.
"The ruling used does not affect the same protocol", says Pierre Noizat, who has just launched Paymium, a real currency payment company that uses the Bitcoin network.
The ECB also takes into account the possibility of anonymous money laundering through this service.
But cash money has the same defect.
The heavyweights, such as Wikipedia, reject such payments.
Others, such as the Wordpress platform, accept them.
Recently, Adi Shamir and Dorit Ron, from the Weizmann Institute in Israel, analyzed the accounting book and showed that about 80% of bitcoins are not circulating.
In November, the "giant sales" were launched.
"30,000 dollars were changed", Jon Holmquist, who works for Coinabul, which converts bitcoins into gold, is delighted.
Pierre Noizat, author of a pedagogical book on that currency, believes quite a lot in the potential of this technology in addition to the network of transactions.
His system, Paytunia, is equivalent to a credit card (in real currency) or a mobile payment without contact, but it uses Bitcoin to validate transactions, which are thus cheaper.
The carrier, in addition, manages his identity and can therefore remain anonymous.
The system is easy to set up in shops, which do not have to install new terminals or software.
All they need is a location that a phone can "photograph and recognize", says Pierre Noizat, who claims to have thousands of users.
There is a general movement to review hierarchical systems for more horizontal systems.
"It will take time for Bitcoin to take over, but in 2013 there will be a change", predicts.
On the other hand, in his report the ECB will re-evaluate the various risks, which are considered high today, in case this currency succeeds.

It is a new double or nothing to the President Mohammed Morsi.

For his opponents, the President continues his "autocratic delirium" and continues to "betray his word" and "trample on the right".
On behalf of his supporters, it is assured that this is a measure to end the institutional and political crisis more quickly and to accelerate the transition process.

A very short time that forces the Brothers to resign from their plan to explain the text, article by article, to the Egyptians.

Considering that this resource has been voted on very quickly, it contains an ultimatum for the Egyptian people: "either vote my text or I keep the full powers", powers that supposedly will end with the adoption of the Constitution.
It is in this strange atmosphere that 85 members of this Constituent Assembly, mostly Islamist, voted the text yesterday.
Most liberals did not attend the call.
In mid-November, a little before the declaration of the constitution, they had closed the door because they thought they could not make their points of view heard.

Salafist parties, for whom the establishment of Islamic law is a fundamental claim, hoped that they could replace "principles" with "norms", which would have allowed a stricter application.

The Higgs boson in detail
The announcement of the possible discovery of the Higgs boson generated a great stir last summer, and for good reason.
It is believed, in fact, that this boson is a participant in the mechanism responsible for the mass of everything that exists in the universe, nothing more and nothing less.

And what is more, it is the particle whose existence the Standard Model predicted: our best or "least good" explanation of the nature and behavior of matter, which has not yet been observed empirically.
But for physicists it is not yet clear that it is Higgs.
We know without a doubt that there is a new particle and that it is very similar to the Higgs boson predicted by the standard model.
In addition, new data released this week at an important physics conference held in Kyoto seem to confirm that it is, although more data is needed to be completely sure.
However, we assume it is Higgs, since the chances of being wrong seem few. We will see what it is.
In this great world, there is a general and inescapable law that implies that two things cannot be found in the same place at the same time.
There is no way to violate that rule and you should not try too hard, because it will end up hurting you.

Although the physics of particles is a very complex world, it has been shown that there is also a law of this kind: the Pauli exclusion principle, which stipulates that two particles cannot occupy the same space at the same time if they are in the same "quantum state"; a "state" that, in
Physicists classify particles into two categories.
On the one hand, we find the good citizens called fermions, who obey wisely the first principle of Pauli.

And there are the anarchists, a dirty panda of anarcho-syndicalists who have no respect for anything, or at least not for this principle, which means that they can be found in the same place and at the same time.

According to the Berkeley Laboratories' web page, the particles are divided into two groups: the mesons, which we will not discuss here, and the "force particles", which are the ones that the great forces of nature propagate through and with which the Higgs boson is somehow related.
These bosons, it should be noted here, are not the exotic creatures that we might think.
In fact, if he can read this article, it is thanks to an extraordinary particle: the photon or the "light particle" that acts as the "message" of the electromagnetic force.
In fact, when a charged particle accelerates or changes direction, it "disorders" the electromagnetic field in that exact vicinity; just like when we throw a stone into a pond.
In this "disorder" an electromagnetic wave (of light, of infrared, of ultraviolet, etc.) is born, and this wave is nothing but a photon; that is, one of the "force carriers" bosons.
More stable field
The same thing happens with the Higgs boson, with the difference that it is another field, the Higgs field, which needs to be "disordered" for this boson to appear.
Now, the Higgs field is much more stable than the electromagnetic field. To activate it, you need to reach extremely high energies, just like trying to slide a big rock across a frozen lake.
Therefore, it is necessary to have a huge particle accelerator like the one at CERN (the great hadron collider is a ring 27 km in circumference) to reach such levels of energy.

With Bitcoin, pay and sell without banks
The opposite to the current exchange rates, based on central banks, the transactions identified and the processing charges between the parties.
In addition, as often happens in technology, the political vision is palpable: the conviction that the current monetary system, composed of bank monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, Bitcoin, invented by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is at the same time a virtual currency that can be converted to dollars, euros, etc. and a secure exchange protocol in the way of BitTorrent, which allows the exchange of files on an equal basis.
Thanks to 15,000 computers on the network, more than 200,000 transactions have been recorded.
And close to a thousand websites accept bitcoins as donations or as a form of payment.
The bitcoin price, after reaching a high of $30 (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to $2 five months later, before returning today to around $10 (the prices are counted on the bitcoincharts.com page).
It is not impressive when compared to the changes in real money or financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (ECB) was interested in it in an October report on virtual currencies.
In it, the bitcoin was described as "the most successful virtual currency", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to the conventional coins".

Bitcoin is different from other systems with types of virtual currencies such as "credits", used to advance in a video game and that can be won by playing or can be bought (and even sometimes exchanged).
The social network Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with the changes.
With Bitcoin, all the nodes of the network are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers of currency and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double-key encryption system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public account book, which is spread throughout the network.
The key point is to write that new transaction in that book.
This is a resolution of a mathematical challenge launched at the computers and the winner, a kind of provisional central bank, will have the privilege of adding that additional line.
It is a phase of file shredding, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique digital signature.
The computers "take" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The goal is to find the number that offers a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes will easily verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then inextricably linked to the chain of other transactions; any modification would change the trace.

Yes, in order to commit a fraud, a user would want to pay twice with the same money very quickly (in less than ten minutes), the network would only accept one of the two transactions; the other would remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will receive 50 bitcoins.
To avoid inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is, therefore, limited to 21 million, but they are divisible to the hundred-millionth, which leaves a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in the power of calculation.
The life of the network has already had its ups and downs.
The websites that offer services for Bitcoin have been attacked and bitcoins have been stolen from the deposit.
"The decision used does not affect the same protocol", says Pierre Noizat, who has just launched Paymium, a real currency payment company that uses the Bitcoin network.
The ECB also takes into account the possibility of anonymous money laundering through this service.

The heavy actors, such as Wikipedia, reject such payments.
Others, such as the Wordpress platform, accept them.

In November, the "giant sales" were launched.

With Bitcoin, pay and sell without banks
The opposite to the current exchange rates based on central banks, the identified transactions and the processing charges between the parties.
In addition, as is often the case with technology, the political vision is palpable: the conviction that the current monetary system, composed of banking monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, Bitcoin, invented by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym), is at the same time a virtual currency convertible to dollars, euros, etc. and a secure exchange protocol in the way of BitTorrent, which allows the exchange of files on an equal basis.
Thanks to 15,000 computers on the network, there have been more than 200,000 transactions recorded.
And close to a thousand websites accept bitcoins as donations or as a form of payment.
The bitcoin price, after reaching a peak of $30 (23 euros) in June 2011, fell to $2 five months later, before returning today to around $10 (the prices are tracked on the bitcoincharts.com page).
It is not impressive when compared to the real world changes in currency or financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (ECB) was interested in it in an October report on virtual currencies.
In it, the bitcoin was described as "the most successful virtual currency", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to conventional coins".

Bitcoin is different from other systems with types of virtual currencies such as "credits", used to advance in a video game and that can be won by playing or can be bought (and even in some cases traded).
The social network Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with the changes.
With bitcoin, all the nodes of the network are at the same time bookkeepers, verifiers, issuers of currency and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two electronic addresses in the form of an email.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is signed electronically through a double-key encryption system.
The network can thus verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public ledger, which is spread throughout the network.
The key point is to write that new transaction in that book.
This is a solution to a mathematical challenge launched at the computers, and the winner, a kind of provisional central banker, will have the privilege of adding that extra line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique numerical signature.
The computers "catch" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The goal is to find the number that offers a particular fingerprint (more zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes will easily verify that it is the good one.
The transaction is then inextricably linked to the chain of other transactions; any change would alter the trace.

Yes, in order to commit a fraud, a user would like to pay twice with the same money very quickly (less than ten minutes), the network will only accept one of the two transactions; the other will remain orphaned, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will be awarded 50 bitcoins.
To avoid inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before the end of 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but they are divisible to the hundred-millionth, which leaves a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in computing power.
The life of the network has already had its ups and downs.
Web sites that offer services for Bitcoin have been attacked and bitcoins have been stolen from deposit.
"The ruling used does not affect the same protocol", says Pierre Noizat, who has just launched Paymium, a real money payment company that uses the Bitcoin network.
The ECB also takes into account the possibility of anonymous money laundering through this service.
But cash money has the same defect.
The heavyweights, such as Wikipedia, reject such payments.
Others, such as the Wordpress platform, accept them.
Recently, Adi Shamir and Dorit Ron, from the Weizmann Institute in Israel, analyzed the book of accounts and showed that around 80% of bitcoins are not circulating.
In November, the "giant sales" were launched.
"30,000 dollars were changed", Jon Holmquist, who works for Coinabul, which converts bitcoins into gold, is delighted.
Pierre Noizat, author of a pedagogical book on that currency, believes quite a lot in the potential of this technology in addition to the network of transactions.
His system, Paytunia, is equivalent to a credit card (in real currency) or a mobile payment without contact, but uses Bitcoin to validate transactions, which are thus cheaper.
The carrier, in addition, manages his identity and can therefore remain anonymous.
The system is easy to set up in shops, which do not have to install new terminals or software.
All they need is a location that a phone can "photograph and recognize", says Pierre Noizat, who claims to have thousands of users.
There is a general movement to review hierarchical systems for more horizontal systems.
"It will take time for Bitcoin to be accepted, but in 2013 there could be a change", predicts.
On the other hand, in his report the ECB will re-evaluate the various risks, which are considered high today, in case this currency succeeds.

A Constitution with a knife in Egypt
It is a new double or nothing to the President Mohammed Morsi.
While Egypt is more divided than ever in terms of the constitutional declaration, which gives it provisional powers, he decided to play the whole for the whole.
The surprise came on Wednesday when he announced that the Constituent Assembly would vote on his final text the next day.
Just a week ago, the Head of State gave two more months to this Assembly to finish its work.
And almost two years ago Egypt has been using a provisional text, several times modified, which weakens the institutional stability and leads to judicial entanglements.
This new initiative has only increased the division in the country.
For his opponents, the President continues his "autocratic delirium" and continues to "betray his word" and "trample on the right".
On behalf of his supporters, it is assured that this is a measure to end the institutional and political crisis more quickly and to accelerate the transition process.
In the next 15 days, a referendum should be organized.
A very short time that forces the Brothers to renounce their project of explaining the text, article by article, to the Egyptians.
For the President, it is also a way to regain popular and democratic legitimacy while the controversy is causing havoc throughout the country.
Mohammed Morsi seems to be convinced that the Egyptians will vote for him, as he said in an interview with the American magazine Time.

Considering that this resource has been voted on very quickly, it contains an ultimatum for the Egyptian people: "either vote my text or I keep the full powers", powers that supposedly will end with the adoption of the Constitution.
It is in this strange atmosphere that 85 members of this Constituent Assembly, mostly Islamist, voted the text yesterday.
Most liberals did not attend the call.
In mid-November, a little before the constitutional declaration, they had closed the door because they thought they could not make their points of view heard.
The representatives of human rights, religious minorities and civil society did the same.
In order to achieve the necessary quorum, 11 members, substitute members, were added hastily this morning.
Some of them are very close to the Muslim Brotherhood.
As was expected, the articles voted on have been voted on unanimously.

On the other hand, the commentators find it amusing that one of the few differences of the day has been expressed practically at the time of prayer, so much so that several members of the committee thought that the clock of the Constituent was wrong.
The text, which was still being voted on yesterday afternoon, consists of 234 articles.
Article 2, the subject of all eyes, is still ultimately identical to that of the 1971 Constitution, which stipulated that "the principles of Sharia constitute the main source of law."
Salafist parties, for whom the establishment of Islamic law is a fundamental claim, hoped that they could replace "principles" with "rules", which would have allowed a more strict application.
For the Islamicists, that this article has not been modified is a guarantee of their good will and respect for the other components of the Egyptian society.
Liberals accuse him of hypocrisy and consider that it is nothing more than a publicity stunt.
According to them, the Islamization of the Constitution is done through other articles.
They refer, in particular, to Article 220, which confers a consultative role on the Al-Azhar University, in particular for anyone who has to confirm their compliance with the laws of Sharia.
According to the Egypt specialist Sophie Pommier, it is worrying because "the people called to speak are not elected and have no democratic legitimacy.
Here we glimpse the premises of a theocracy.
The fears of the liberals are also increased by the fact that the next university rector will be much less moderate than the current one.
"At the moment, there is no concrete religious implication.
With this Constitution, we are in the civil state.

The majority of the lawyers who have been working on that text are not ulemas but university graduates, some of them trained in the French system, says Alexis Blouet, who is preparing a thesis on the Egyptian constitutional transition.
However, he admits that there may be some ambiguity around Article 220, as the terms used imitate the religious vocabulary.
"We are specifically referring to the term iqh [Islamic jurisprudence, ndlr].
And the question that could be asked in the future would be to what extent are the civil judges competent to speak for all this.
Beyond its religious character, the text voted yesterday has received many criticisms that refer to the powers extended to the President of the Republic.
The Muslim Brothers will claim that they are few in comparison with those who were during the previous regime.
Another point of contention: the powers granted to the army.
In accordance with the desire of the military, the review of the Defense budget will not be submitted to Parliament, but to a National Defense Council.
Military tribunals will not be allowed to try civilians, as demanded by human rights organizations.
These also showed their concerns about the text, which they consider a death sentence.
The crime of blasphemy is still in force and, from now on, insults are prohibited, which could lead to serious consequences for freedom of expression, especially for the press.
In addition, no article emphasizes the protection of women, says Heba Morayef, of Human Rights Watch.
According to her, the only positive thing has been the prohibition of torture in accordance with Article 36.
